absent: Numeric values of register-count, breakpoint-count, register numbers, breakpoint lengths, and debug-register encodings.
Layouts of trap frame, inactive task frame, die arguments, software breakpoint record, probe, control block, and perf attributes.
Semantics of perf breakpoint install, uninstall, restore, reserve, release, and wide registration.
Behavior of generic helpers for exception handling, hex parsing, removed-breakpoint test, NMI callback, and text patching.
Meanings of exception vectors, error codes, NMI vectors, notifier return codes, and watchdog effects.
Kprobes out-of-line execution model and exception-table lookup semantics.
Opcode attribute classification and prefix iteration order.

findings.text: Register accessors expose numbered debugger register read and write over a trap frame, translating numbers through a descriptor table and handling a special system-call number register.

Descriptor table pairs each debugger number with a short name plus a byte width and a trap-frame offset, using a negative offset to mark unavailable segment entries; widths and ordering differ between 32-bit and 64-bit builds.

Register writes are refused for the stack pointer and the system-call number entry on all builds and for three segment entries on 32-bit; otherwise bytes are copied only when the descriptor offset is valid and success is always reported.

Register reads serve the system-call number entry from its dedicated trap-frame field, reject out-of-range numbers with a null result, copy only when the descriptor offset is valid, force a constant selector value for two segment entries on 32-bit, and return the entry name.
Sleeping-task conversion builds a debugger register array for a non-running thread from its saved stack pointer and inactive frame.

Synthesized sleeping state zeroes most general and extended entries and the program counter, copies the thread stack pointer, derives the frame pointer from the inactive frame, and installs kernel selector plus cleared flag values with width handling specific to each build.

Hardware breakpoint store is a fixed-size array where each slot holds an enabled flag with an address plus length and type encodings and a per-CPU event pointer; a separate scalar accumulates early debug-control bits.

Breakpoint correction skips disabled slots and then follows an early path that programs debug registers directly while accumulating control bits or a late path that refreshes disabled perf attributes and installs them before a global restore.

Slot reservation and release walk online CPUs to reserve or release each per-CPU event, do nothing while early, unwind already-reserved CPUs on reservation failure, and signal failure on release so the caller can retry.
Hardware breakpoint management offers set, single remove by address, and bulk remove operations over the slot array.

Setting finds the first disabled slot, maps generic execution and data watch kinds to processor execution, write, and access encodings with execution forcing unit length, accepts only supported lengths with widest length limited to 64-bit, and enables only after successful reservation.

Single removal matches address among enabled slots and clears enabled only after slot release; bulk removal and temporary disable uninstall active perf events and mark them disabled, else clear early mask bits or release slots, with disable also resetting the debug control register.
CPU roundup broadcasts a non-maskable interrupt to all other processors to force them into the debugger.

Remote command handling for continue, step, detach, and kill optionally updates the program counter from a supplied parameter, always clears the trace flag and the stepping-CPU marker, then re-arms both only for step; other commands request continued handling elsewhere.
A step that transitions from kernel to user context is consumed with a diagnostic and resumed through continue handling while clearing the branch-step status bit carried in the error slot.

Non-maskable dispatch treats a local event as a debugger roundup only while a debugger session is active, recording the CPU and servicing the watchdog, and treats an unknown event as completion of a prior debug entry; all other cases report not-handled.

Die-chain entry filters user-mode traps and user single-step activity, delegates kernel debug and other traps to the generic exception handler, services the watchdog on debugger entry, and is wrapped with interrupt save-restore plus a low-level trap gate on I/O registration.

Architecture setup registers a die notifier followed by local and unknown non-maskable handlers with ordered unwinding on failure; teardown unregisters breakpoint resources then both non-maskable handlers then the die notifier.

Late setup preallocates one wide breakpoint per slot with a disabled unit-length write attribute anchored at the setup routine, arms a unit sample period with an overflow callback, and clears destroy handling while releasing the slot.
Overflow callback sets virtual debug-status trap bits in the current thread for each enabled slot.
Trap-address helpers adjust breakpoint trap addresses, assign a new program counter, and insert or remove software breakpoints with a fallback path when direct text update fails.

Direct text patching for breakpoint insert and remove is used only when the kernel text lock is free, otherwise a fault-tolerant copy path is used; die dispatch runs with interrupts saved and restored.
Architecture operations record links a one-byte breakpoint pattern with a hardware-breakpoint capability flag and callbacks for set, remove, temporary disable, bulk remove, and correction.
Software breakpoint instruction encoding is one byte with decimal value 204.

Probe entry and exit sequences preserve general registers around handler execution while skipping trap-frame header fields; the 64-bit form covers extended registers and the 32-bit form covers segment registers with different skip widths.
Detour setup reports success without action and optimized-probe recovery returns its input address unchanged in these fragments.
Per-CPU probe state consists of a current-probe pointer initially null and a control block instance.
A bitmap records which two-byte opcodes may execute out of line, a row-combining helper builds its words, and a blacklist excludes the task-switch routine with a null terminator.
Relative branch synthesis writes a five-byte branch or call at a destination by computing displacement from the end of the source to the target and storing the supplied opcode.

Out-of-line eligibility rejects fault-prone addresses, consults the two-byte bitmap for two-byte opcodes, requires single-byte opcodes otherwise, rejects address-size and certain segment prefixes, denies control-transfer and privileged opcode groups, and filters grouped opcodes by their register field.
Failed hardware-breakpoint removal leaves the slot enabled for a caller retry, and failed late breakpoint allocation tears down debugger registration.
User-mode traps and user single-step activity bypass debugger handling, preventing user execution from entering the kernel debugger path.
Common probe header defines an inclusion guard macro.
